transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is that I’ve gotten sort of… stuck in these little routines, and they’re not huge dramatic things, but they’ve started interfering with my day. Like, if I handle my wrist brace, I feel like I need to wash my hands again, even if I know I just washed them or that it’s probably fine.

And then there’s the checking. Before I leave, I’ll go back and look at the stove, and then the front door, sometimes more than once. I’ll tell myself, “You already checked it,” but then I get this nagging feeling and I go back anyway. I also find myself silently counting through steps before I can leave, almost like I have to get it right before I’m allowed to go.

It sounds small when I say it out loud, but it’s making me late to things, and that’s what finally made me think I should come talk to someone. Even when part of me knows I’ve done enough, I can’t seem to just stop and move on.
Do you feel anxious or upset if you try to skip one of these routines or checking behaviors?

Yes… I do. I mean, I wouldn’t say it’s a full panic or anything, but I get very unsettled if I try to just leave it alone. Like with the wrist brace—if I handle it and then tell myself, “No, you don’t need to wash again, you just washed,” there’s this uncomfortable feeling that sort of sits there and keeps pulling at me until I go wash my hands anyway.

And with leaving the house, if I don’t recheck the stove or the front door, I’ll start walking away and then my mind keeps going back to it. I’ll think, “Did I really check it properly? Did I miss something?” Even when I know, logically, that I already looked. The counting is similar—I’ll be going through the steps in my head, and if I try to skip that or cut it short, it feels like I haven’t finished the leaving process, if that makes sense.

It’s not that I want to spend the extra time doing it. It actually frustrates me, because I know I’ve done enough. But if I don’t do the routine, I feel tense and distracted, and then I usually give in just so I can feel settled enough to move on. That’s when it makes me late.

The insight-oriented response and the nature of the compulsions make F42.2 (OCD, with good or fair insight) the most accurate code.
